Answer: B
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) demonstrates that the large opacity is located in the anterior chest wall/soft tissues rather than within the lung parenchyma, indicating an extrapulmonary lesion. Extrapulmonary soft tissue masses typically displace or compress adjacent structures without causing primary bone destruction, unlike invasive pulmonary malignancies.
